newsitem.title: GERMANY: Hoechst says no decision yet on pharma unit.
newsitem.headline: Hoechst says no decision yet on pharma unit.

text.p: German chemicals group Hoechst AG does not have to decide whether to float its pharmaceutical unit Hoechst Marion Roussel (HMR) on the market in the current year, Hoechst chief executive Juergen Dormann said on Tuesday.

Dormann said the option to bring the unit to market remained open and was one of a number of possibilities open to Hoechst, Dormann said in an advance release of next Friday's edition of "manager" magazine.
Dormann said the future for Hoechst's pharmaceuticals business lay in technological advance.
"We need technological breakthroughs, which we can then patent, because the future does not lie in 'me-too' products or generic products," Dormann said.
He also said a partnership with Glaxo Wellcome or Pharmacia and Upjohn could help boost growth.

"We have examined the main focus points of our research strategy and newly defined them. We are not exactly happy with new products in the pipeline, but we are more confident than we were a couple of years ago," said Dormann.
Dormann said that products still to be licensed and products still in development would bring growth of six to eight percent in coming years.
